report.title: 2025 Water Quality Report - NASA Ames Research Center, Moffett Field, California (July 2026)

sources_described: Drinking water at NASA Ames is supplied by the San Francisco Regional Water System (SFRWS), owned and operated by the SFPUC: Hetch Hetchy surface water (unfiltered; UV and chlorine disinfection, pH adjustment, fluoridation, chloramination) plus Sunol Valley Water Treatment Plant filtered water; upcountry non-Hetch Hetchy sources and groundwater wells were not used in 2025, and the SFRWS imported a very small amount (0.38%) of treated water from Valley Water in April and May 2025. NASA Ames does not use groundwater.

violations: No exceedances of drinking water standards were identified in any of the samples collected at NASA Ames in 2025 (page 3; footnote 1: all results met State and Federal drinking water health standards).

Monitoring violation disclosed on behalf of the supplier (page 3): the San Francisco Regional Water System, operated by SFPUC, failed to monitor for recycled filter backwash water turbidity at its Sunol Valley Water Treatment Plant from June 23, 2025 to July 2, 2025 because of a turbidimeter equipment failure; corrected July 3, 2025; the SFPUC states it was not an emergency and did not impact water quality.

Lead and copper tap monitoring (page 5, footnote 7): in the September 2023 round, 2 of 22 site samples (Buildings M583C and N200) had lead above the Action Level of 15 ppb; the 90th percentile (10.4 ppb) was below the AL so no regulatory violation occurred. N200 fountains are fitted with NSF/ANSI-certified lead-removing filters; M583C is abandoned and scheduled for demolition.
extraction_notes: Single supplier (SFPUC/SFRWS) so no per-source columns; the only source-specific rows are the three turbidity rows (Unfiltered Hetch Hetchy vs. Filtered SVWTP water), which carry source_group. Table header is 'Range or Level Found' and 'Average or [Max]'; bracketed values are maxima and are stored as value with basis 'highest single result'. The non-regulated parameters table on page 9 is internally inconsistent as printed: Alkalinity and Total Organic Carbon share 8 - 131 / 61, Boron and Silica share 3.1 - 29 / 16, and Hardness 0.2 - 10 ppm cannot be reconciled with Calcium <20 - 281 ppm and Magnesium 7.06 - 9.6 ppm; all values copied exactly as printed and flagged in notes. '<x' range lows and 'ND' are stored as 0 with the printed form in notes. Lead and copper are 2023 triennial results (next 2026) reported in ppb. The treated-water fluoride entry comes from footnote 5 (page 10), not the table, and its printed average (0.2) lies outside its printed range (0.5-0.8). Tables verified against rendered images of pages 8 and 9.
